correctness.rationale: The two-coordinate recurrence counts nonempty patterns as X+Y-2 and preserves gcd; every primitive modular state is reached by coprime lifts and Euclidean subtraction. A self-loop makes every K_m-block kernel entry at least δ^K_m even with time-varying biases, so minorization proves the stated total variation bound. Inclusion-exclusion produces the precise r+2 projection. Literal brute counts for 8191 binary words, exact primitive state fibers for m=2..24, and 45 weighted cases independently support the algebra. Every infinite claim follows from proof, not from finite experiments.

originality.rationale: The proved content extends the classical uniform-level Stern residue distribution from fair binary levels to arbitrary independent, non-identically distributed uniformly elliptic bits, with one explicit rate over all schedules, exact arithmetic residue masses, and a boundary example. Full-text comparisons with Reznick, Żak and the random-subsequence expectation work exclude their already known fair-source and arithmetic prerequisites. General finite-state minorization is acknowledged as classical; no known inspected published result directly supplies the inhomogeneous statement. Residual risk: general random matrix-product and stochastic mixing literature may subsume it.
residual_risks: A stronger theorem on arbitrary products of positive weighted permutation kernels or random continued fractions could already imply the statement after its classical Stern encoding.
Full-text search of the broader literature cannot establish uniqueness; the generic Doeblin contraction lemma is classical and could make the new specialization appear routine to some experts.

value.rationale: The residue of the actual distinct-subsequence count is a natural string statistic with nonuniform arithmetic bias. A universal limiting law is valid across all independent time-varying Bernoulli sources with probabilities in a common compact subinterval of (0,1), beyond the known fair/uniform-level Stern distribution. An explicit all-bias convergence rate and an example showing why ellipticity matters answer concrete robustness and boundary questions rather than an arbitrary finite census.
